sources.title: Aditya Guntuboyina, Lecture Notes for 201A Fall 2019

contents.name: §5.5, Theorem 5.5.1: identity-covariance Gaussian idempotent quadratic forms have chi-square law
contents.reason: The local theorem proves the projection result from an orthogonal eigenbasis and additionally supplies independence of both vector components and squared norms.

contents.name: §5.5, Example 5.5.2: normal sample mean and residual sum are independent, with chi-square residual sum
contents.reason: The local proof derives the sample decomposition and exact t pivot, including the positive residual denominator and coverage event.

contents.name: §5.5, Example 5.5.3: equicorrelated Gaussian sample mean and residual sum
contents.reason: This covariance-specific example is outside the assigned identity-covariance projection and exact-t interface; no equicorrelation result is claimed.

contents.name: §5.6, Theorem 5.6.1: chi-square law for a standard Gaussian quadratic form defined by an idempotent matrix
contents.reason: This is the same projection quadratic-form claim, locally proved with the complement and component-independence statements made explicit.

contents.name: §5.6, Theorem 5.6.2: converse characterization of chi-square quadratic forms by idempotence
contents.reason: The converse needs a separate moment-generating-function argument and is not part of the assigned Gaussian projection, t, or F claims.

contents.name: §5.6, Theorem 5.6.3: general-covariance quadratic-form chi-square criterion
contents.reason: The covariance-weighted criterion has additional matrix hypotheses and is beyond the assigned fixed-design normal projection results.

contents.name: §5.6, Example 5.6.4: scaled identity-covariance idempotent quadratic form
contents.reason: The local regression theorem explicitly standardizes by σ² and proves the residual chi-square law under positive residual degrees.

contents.name: §5.6, Example 5.6.5: equicorrelated Gaussian residual quadratic form
contents.reason: This covariance-structure example is outside the fixed-design independent-error model and is not used to support its exact F statement.

contents.name: §5.6, Example 5.6.6: Mahalanobis quadratic form
contents.reason: This full-rank covariance quadratic form is not required for the assigned t/F pivot claims and is not imported.

sources.title: Yen-Chi Chen, UW STAT 512 Lecture 8: Linear Models and Multivariate Normal Distributions
sources.locator: Complete 11-page lecture note read; §8.4.1 and the immediately following normalizing, projection, and IID-normal discussions, PDF pp.9–11.

contents.name: §8.4.1 Chi-square distribution: squared norm of a standard multivariate normal
contents.reason: The local definition fixes zero degrees separately and proves positive-degree density and denominator positivity instead of relying on a formula alone.

contents.name: Normalizing a Gaussian vector: standardized Mahalanobis norm has chi-square law
contents.reason: The general covariance inverse quadratic form is not part of the assigned identity-covariance orthogonal projection and t/F development.

contents.name: Projection property: a rank-m projection of a standard Gaussian has a chi-square quadratic form
contents.reason: The local theorem covers endpoint ranks and also proves independence of the projected and complementary vectors.

contents.name: IID normals: sample mean and sample variance independence and chi-square residual law
contents.reason: The local result adds the exact t ratio, quantile inversion, and coverage proof with n≥2 and σ>0 stated.

sources.title: Dmitry Panchenko, MIT 18.443 Statistics for Applications, Fall 2003, Lectures 16–17
sources.locator: Complete 139-page course-note PDF read; Lecture 16.1, printed pp.60–61 (PDF pp.67–68), and Lecture 17.1, printed pp.63–66 (PDF pp.70–73).

contents.name: Lecture 16.1, Fisher and Student distributions: F ratio of independent chi-square sums
contents.reason: The local definitions fix positive degrees, specify product-law realizations, and prove the denominator is positive almost surely.

contents.name: Lecture 17.1, confidence intervals for parameters of a normal distribution: exact t pivot and central mean interval
contents.reason: The local proof supplies the orthogonal projection independence argument and derives exact coverage from the pivot and unique symmetric quantiles.

contents.name: Lecture 17, worked n=10 normal-sample mean and variance intervals
contents.reason: The numerical data set and variance interval are not part of this batch; the B page instead computes a separate four-observation mean interval.

sources.title: MIT 18.S096, Regression Analysis, Lecture 6: Distribution Theory: Normal Regression Models
sources.locator: Complete 45-page lecture PDF read; “Distribution Theory: Normal Regression Models,” PDF p.34.

contents.name: Theorem for the normal linear regression model, parts (a)–(d): coefficient/residual independence, residual chi-square law, and t statistics
contents.reason: The local QR proof independently derives the exact law. The printed part (d) denominator is missing a square root: it gives σ̂ Cjj, while the correct standard error is σ̂√Cjj; the local theorem uses and proves the corrected expression.

sources.title: Dmitry Panchenko, MIT 18.443 Statistics for Applications, Fall 2006, Lecture 4: Multivariate normal distribution and multivariate CLT
sources.locator: Complete 4-page lecture note read; “Orthogonal transformation of an i.i.d. standard normal sample,” PDF p.4.

contents.name: Orthogonal transformation of an i.i.d. standard normal sample: the transformed coordinates remain independent standard normals
contents.reason: The local proof reaches this claim by characteristic functions and finite-Borel Fourier uniqueness. The source’s Jacobian paragraph has a sign defect at PDF p.4: it says det(V)=1, while the correct identity is |det(V)|=1; the local proof does not use that change-of-variables argument.
